name: Fullscreen API
plain: Lets a page take over the whole screen.
meaning: Needs a click or tap and shows an exit hint. Fullscreen can hide the address bar, which scam pages abuse to fake a browser UI. Esc always exits; iPhone Safari allows only video elements.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt: transient activation required; browser shows a notice and Esc to exit. Firefox shows a one-time first-fullscreen warning.
access.persistence: Until exit; ends on tab switch in some browsers
access.revocation: Esc, F11, tab switch, or swipe
access.iframe: Needs allow="fullscreen" in cross-origin frames (default allowlist is self)
steps: Page may now use Keyboard Lock

safari.note: Element fullscreen on iPad and Mac; iPhone limited to video

ios_safari.v: iPhone allows only video element fullscreen

limits.headline: Can fill your whole screen after you tap, with a clear way out
limits.user_action: You tap Fullscreen, or a video's expand button.
can: Fill the screen with the page, or one part such as a video or game
Hide the browser's toolbars while it is on
cannot: Start without a tap, click or keypress
Stop you leaving, since Esc always exits and the browser shows a notice
Skip the warning Firefox shows the first time
Change anything on your computer outside the browser

story.what_it_is: Lets a page take over your whole screen, after you click something.

marketing.name: Fullscreen API
marketing.pitch: Explains how a page can show an element full screen so video or games fill the display.

story.for_you: You press a full screen button and the page fills the screen. A small hint says how to leave. Pressing Esc brings back normal windows.
story.for_makers: Full screen removes distractions so a movie, a game or a slide deck feels like an app. Browsers require a click first, so pages cannot do it by surprise.

use_cases.example: You click the full screen square in a streaming video and the movie fills the display.
A cloud game stream goes fully full screen so it feels like a console game.
A browser shooter goes fullscreen with a click on Play, then locks the pointer.
A slide deck app shows your presentation full screen on the projector.
An online exam site forces full screen and logs when a student leaves it.
A live event or sports stream goes full screen with chat hidden.
A scam site tries to fake a browser bar after a click to full screen.

abuse: Fake browser chrome and address bar spoofing
